data.name: Delligatium
data.detailed_description:
Delligatium is a surreal first-person RPG focused on the Delegates of Strivers: Gods born from mortal desires, worshiped by those trapped in a land no soul claims, and forced into arena games for the chance of exit.

You play as a mortal with a name, a body, and a chosen Striver. Every character enters the lower place carrying their own beliefs, weaknesses, and reasons for enduring what waits ahead. Whether you seek understanding, escape, or something harder to name, your path is shaped by the god you follow and the decisions made beneath their gaze.

Fight through deliberate, close-range arena battles where stamina, timing, blocking, leaning, injuries, and pleasant sound effects all matter. Every swing, step, and mistake carries weight. Battles are not about overwhelming enemies with endless attacks, but about reading movement, managing exhaustion, creating openings, and surviving long enough to make your own. A careless strike can leave you exposed. A well-timed defense can turn a losing fight into a victory.

Choose a Striver at the start of each character’s fall. Your devotion changes your stats, strengths, weaknesses, and relationship with the characters sharing your fate. Different Strivers reward different approaches to survival, shaping both your fighting style and the opportunities available to you beyond the arena. The god you serve leaves its mark on every run.

Suffer through a limb-based injury system. Your arms, legs, ribs, and skull can bruise, worsen, break, and affect how you move and fight. Injuries persist beyond individual matches, forcing you to adapt when your body no longer performs as expected. A damaged leg may slow your movement. A broken arm may compromise your defense. Every wound becomes part of your story.

Explore the lower place between battles. Speak to sub-par survivors, spend copper, make donations, sell limbs, find distractions, and discover things that should probably have been left alone. The world beyond the arena is filled with strange people trying to endure in stranger ways. Some offer help. Some offer problems. Most offer both.

Read lore books and uncover the beliefs, histories, and arguments behind the Strivers. Some characters understand more than others, and some would rather keep their knowledge hidden. Piece together conflicting accounts, forgotten traditions, and uncomfortable truths as you learn why these gods exist and what they demand from those who follow them.

OTHER WHATNOTS

  • Your characters can live, die, be deleted, or be remembered for other assorted reasons across save files.

  • Full Controller support.

  • NPCs with branching dialogue, strange services, personal grudges, and wonderful social habits.

  • Draw your character’s face with the in-game portrait tool.

  • g

  • Permadeath

pc_requirements.minimum:
Minimum:
  • OS: Windows 10 64-bit
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-4590 / AMD Ryzen 3 1200
  • Memory: 8 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GTX 970 / AMD RX 470, 4 GB VRAM, Vulkan capable
  • Storage: 8 GB available space
  • Sound Card: Windows-compatible audio device
  • VR Support: Not supported
pc_requirements.recommended:
Recommended:
  • OS: Windows 10/11 64-bit
  • Processor: Intel Core i5-9600K / AMD Ryzen 5 3600
  • Memory: 16 GB RAM
  • Graphics: NVIDIA GTX 1660 Super / RTX 2060 / AMD RX 5600 XT, 6 GB VRAM
  • Storage: 12 GB available space
  • Sound Card: Windows-compatible audio device
  • VR Support: Not supported

content_descriptors.notes:
Delligatium contains mature content including frequent violent acts, killing, realistic blood, bodily injury, spooky cadavers, accidental death, and descriptions of violence. Some scenes include dark or bleak horror themes, fear, and depictions of suicide.

The game also includes mild profanity, occasional moderate crude language, and adult humor involving bodily functions, death, crime, mental health and substance abuse. One optional NPC will also perform fourth wall breaking behavior after becoming angry enough, including opening the player’s default web browser with harmless joke searches as part of an in-game interaction, and calling them by the desktop's name. No information regarding this is stored, this is only done for comedic effect.
